title: claude t3
prompt: Create ledgerkit/cache.py with class TTLCache(maxsize, ttl, clock=time.monotonic). Methods: put(key, value), get(key, default=None), __len__, __contains__, and a stats() method returning a dict with hits, misses and evictions. It is an LRU cache: when full, put evicts the least recently used live entry, counted as an eviction. Entries expire ttl seconds after their last put; get refreshes LRU order but not expiry. An entry is expired once clock() - stored_time >= ttl. Expired entries are never returned, do not count in len, and must be dropped before any LRU eviction so that a live entry is not evicted while an expired one exists; dropping an expired entry is not an eviction. put on an existing key replaces the value, restarts its ttl and refreshes order. get on a missing or expired key counts a miss. __contains__ does not change order or stats. Raise ValueError if maxsize < 1 or ttl <= 0. All methods must be safe under concurrent threads. Add tests in tests/test_cache.py and run python3 -m pytest -q.
summary:
I added `TTLCache` in `ledgerkit/cache.py` and its tests in `tests/test_cache.py`, and committed both as e2b2dc6 on `crew/1107-616f79`. `python3 -m pytest -q` reports 10 passed, covering the existing `test_money.py` and the new cache tests.

The cache follows your spec. Details worth knowing:
- **Locking:** every method takes an `RLock`, which makes it safe under concurrent threads.
- **Cost of the expiry sweep:** `put` of a new key and `__len__` scan all entries to drop expired ones, so they are O(n) in the number of entries. That is fine at small sizes but would be slow for very large caches.
- **Thread-safety test:** it runs 8 threads of mixed `put`, `get` and `len` calls. It checks that the cache stays within `maxsize` and that hits plus misses add up. It is a smoke test, not proof that there are no races.
